page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.2-8 is an Arm-based virtual machine configured with 4 vCPUs and 8 GB of memory. Powered by the Ampere AmpereOne processor family running at a base clock of 3.0 GHz, this configuration allocates 4 physical cores with one hardware thread per core. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures that workloads do not contend with simultaneous multithreading threads, yielding consistent instruction execution cycles across all available Arm64 cores.

The instance provides 2.0 GB of RAM per core, reflecting a 1:2 compute-optimized vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent data retention. Furthermore, there are no hardware accelerators or GPUs included on this profile. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external ingress and egress.

From an efficiency perspective, the AmpereOne Arm64 architecture delivers an advantageous compute density per allocated core compared to legacy x86 architectures. However, operational tradeoffs include the absence of onboard NVMe storage and the lower RAM density, which restricts the instance from hosting large in-memory databases without scaling up the resource shape. Software must also be compiled or targeted for the aarch64 instruction set.

VM.Standard.A2.Flex.2-8 is best suited for compute-bound tasks that match its 1:2 memory profile, such as microservices, web application serving, native Arm software compilation, automated build testing, and stateless API backends.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.2-8 is an Arm64 compute instance providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Ampere AmpereOne cores operating at 3.0 GHz. Equipped with 8 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a 1:2 core-to-memory distribution suited for compute-focused tasks. The hardware profile excludes dedicated local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for persistent disk I/O. It comes configured with one complimentary public IPv4 address. The non-hyperthreaded single-thread-per-core design avoids shared resource contention, presenting predictable performance per vCPU on Arm-native software environments. The qualitative trade-off centers on its modest memory headroom and reliance on external network volumes, making it most appropriate for microservices, lightweight web servers, containerized application components, and continuous integration pipelines targeting the aarch64 instruction set.
